text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا۟ بَأْسَنَا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَحْدَهُۥ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِۦ مُشْرِكِينَ

words.gloss_range: prefixed consequential connector opening the temporal response scene

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: temporal threshold particle opening the seeing-response frame

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) launches the ayah as consequence rather than reset. It draws the whole {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}})-scene into the aftermath of the prior surrounding judgment (40:83), so the later confession is already framed as speech forced by what has caught up with them.

topics.headline: consequence-bound opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as the next consequence of the surrounding judgment in the prior scene (40:83), not as a fresh conversion scene.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a prefixed conjunction, and attachment evidence makes the following temporal clause the setting for the speech response.

topics.headline: sequel and threshold fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices cause and timing compressed into the opening unit before any verb appears.
topics.reason: The prefixed connector is attached to the temporal particle, so sequence, consequence, and threshold are heard together.

topics.headline: clipped onset has no separate payoff
topics.reason: The acoustic observation repeats the already retained quick consequential onset without adding a separate lexical or structural payoff.

words.gloss_range: temporal threshold particle meaning when or once in a completed seeing-response frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Our severity as the explicit object of seeing

words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) makes the speech wait until the sight-event is complete: once they saw, they said. The local construction is temporal, not a not-yet construction, so timing itself weighs against the confession; it begins only after exposure to {{ar:بَأْسَنَا}} ({{tr:bāʾsanā}}).

topics.headline: completed sight triggers speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is grammatically downstream from completed exposure to punishment.
topics.reason: The temporal particle governs the perfect seeing clause and links it to the following speech clause.

topics.headline: threshold sense, not not-yet sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a threshold force: once they saw, they spoke; the particle is not denying that the sight happened.
topics.reason: The local clause contains a completed perfect verb and a response clause, so the temporal-condition reading is selected over another constructional value.

topics.headline: exposure to speech to repudiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole ayah is organized around exposure first and confession afterward.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the opening temporal clause govern the transition into the full quoted response.

topics.headline: held threshold sound is decorative
topics.reason: The acoustic hold restates the retained threshold idea without a separate reader-facing payoff.

words.gloss_range: completed plural seeing with an explicit punitive object
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, recognizing, and forming judgment; locally narrowed to direct witnessed recognition of divine severity

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Our severity as the explicit object of seeing

words.prose: {{ar:رَأَوْا۟}} ({{tr:raʾaw}}) carries the prior group as plural seers and immediately takes {{ar:بَأْسَنَا}} ({{tr:bāʾsanā}}) as its object. The result is not a vague awakening: sight becomes recognition of a named divine force, and the order makes their later creed reactive. The same seeing-punishment frame is answered by the nonbenefit verdict in the next ayah (40:85).

topics.headline: plural subject becomes witness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punished group is carried in the verb ending and becomes witness against itself before it speaks.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect active third-person plural verb with an implicit plural subject; attachment evidence links it to the same punished peoples.

topics.headline: sight has a named punitive object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not describe vague realization; it has Our severity as its explicit object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following word the direct object of the seeing verb.

topics.headline: sight becomes recognition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices recognition arriving through forced sight rather than through instruction or reflection.
topics.reason: The root range supports visual perception and recognition, while the local object fixes the recognition around divine severity.

topics.headline: direct seeing, not causative showing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the group as direct seers, while divine agency is carried by the possessed object rather than by a causative verb form.
topics.reason: The local form is Form I active perfect, not a causative disclosure form.

topics.headline: seeing anticipates nonbenefit verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same seeing-punishment frame continues into the verdict that belated faith does not benefit (40:85).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete next-ayah recurrence, and local grammar already makes seeing precede the confession.

topics.headline: perception precedes speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices chronology testing the confession before the doctrine is even heard.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence orders the seeing clause before the speech-reporting clause.

topics.headline: audible catch has no separate payoff
topics.reason: The sound observation decorates the already retained break from denial into forced perception.

words.gloss_range: Our severity as the explicit object seen by the punished group
words.root_gloss_range: severity, might, force, and distress; locally the possessed punitive force encountered by sight
words.prose: {{ar:بَأْسَنَا}} ({{tr:bāʾsanā}}) is the thing they see: Our severity, not an unnamed disaster. The possessed form blocks recoding the crisis as accident, and the root range lets the severity be felt as both force exerted and distress suffered. It stands before their own repeated we-claims and becomes the threshold named again when late faith is ruled useless (40:85).

topics.headline: severity as the seen object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine severity is the object encountered before any saving-sounding speech begins.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this verbal noun the explicit object of the seeing verb.

topics.headline: Our severity, not accident
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the crisis as explicitly divine, set against the speakers repeated we-claims.
topics.reason: The first-person plural possessive suffix marks the severity as belonging to the divine speaker.

topics.headline: force felt as distress
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment as both force exerted and distress suffered, while the local noun remains the seen severity rather than an adjective for the people.
topics.reason: The root range supports severity, might, and distress; the local gerund object selects the punitive event-object.

topics.headline: verbal noun packages punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices severity packaged as the thing seen rather than narrated as a separate unfolding action.
topics.reason: QAC tags the form as a gerund or verbal noun in object position.

topics.headline: same severity becomes verdict threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that seeing Our severity sets up the next ayah where faith at that point no longer benefits (40:85).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete recurrence in the following ayah, and the local object marks the trigger point.

topics.headline: severity before we-speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Our severity placed before their repeated we-speech and their safety-colored faith claim.
topics.reason: The local sequence places the possessed severity before first-person confession verbs, making the morphology contrastive.

topics.headline: abrasive sound has no separate payoff
topics.reason: The sound description does not add beyond the retained severity-and-distress payoff.

words.gloss_range: completed plural saying that introduces the full direct confession
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, and claim; locally a recorded utterance after exposure, not proof of accepted belief
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) turns the response into a quoted record. The verb carries the seers into speech and governs the whole confession through the final identity word, so the ayah reports what they claim, not an inward state already accepted; the claim itself is left for the nonbenefit verdict in 40:85. Its one-way Form I speech also resembles crisis confession after exposure, with 10:90 as a concrete delayed-belief parallel.

topics.headline: completed speech record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the whole confession as recorded utterance, not as an inner state report.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the speech verb govern the full direct utterance through the final word.

topics.headline: saying as evidence, not proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quote attempts reversal by saying it, while the next ayah will judge that claim.
topics.reason: The local form reports utterance; it does not itself verify sincerity or benefit.

topics.headline: seers become speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same plural group moving from seeing to first-person confession.
topics.reason: The third-person plural speech verb follows the third-person plural seeing verb and introduces first-person plural verbs inside the quote.

topics.headline: one-way utterance, not dialogue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a one-way crisis confession, not a negotiated exchange.
topics.reason: The local Form I speech verb does not select reciprocal speech morphology.

topics.headline: delayed confession parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a concrete parallel to crisis belief voiced only after exposure, as in the delayed confession of 10:90.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide the concrete 10:90 comparison, and local order likewise places speech after sight.

topics.headline: speech becomes self-indicting record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the quote as a record in which human self-description becomes part of judgment.
topics.reason: The quoted complement includes present claims and the final admission of former identity.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural Form IV claim of belief with a following prepositional complement
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, and belief; locally professed belief in God, with safety pressure from the punishment context

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition routing the belief claim to its complement
proper divine name as the governed belief complement

words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنَّا}} ({{tr:āmannā}}) is a completed we-claim of belief, but its grammar routes that belief through the following {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) toward {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}). The root family lets safety pressure be heard under punishment, while the local Form IV still selects professed belief. The positive claim immediately pairs with a repudiation, and its lateness points toward the nonbenefit verdict (40:85) and the delayed-belief pattern of 10:90.

topics.headline: belief routed by complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices faith taking a governed relation to God rather than a loose direct object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following prepositional phrase the complement of the belief verb.

topics.headline: completed we-belief claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the claim as communal and complete-sounding, even though it arrives late.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect active first-person plural Form IV verb.

topics.headline: belief colored by sought safety
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a safety pressure around the faith claim, while local grammar keeps belief as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The root family includes security and trust, but the local Form IV with a governed complement selects professed belief.

topics.headline: entry into faith, not granting security
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speakers claiming entry into faith, not presenting themselves as ones who grant security.
topics.reason: The surface is Form IV perfect, not a security-giving frame.

topics.headline: faith paired with repudiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the positive claim immediately pushes toward a negative repudiation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the later rejection verb with the belief verb inside the same quote.

topics.headline: late faith under punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this belief claim as part of the Quranic pattern of confession after punishment appears, including 10:90 and the verdict in 40:85.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references, and local timing places the claim after seeing divine severity.

words.gloss_range: prefixed preposition governing the divine name as belief complement
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is not instrumental here; it is the required relation after the belief verb. It makes the divine name the governed content of the claim, so the first declaration is grammatically anchored rather than left as a vague statement of belief.

topics.headline: preposition binds belief to its object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition as the grammatical route by which belief reaches the divine name.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following divine name the governed complement of the belief verb.

topics.headline: link sound repeats binding
topics.reason: The acoustic linking observation duplicates the retained grammatical binding of the preposition.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name governed by the preceding belief preposition
words.root_gloss_range: worship-authority and deity field; locally the proper divine name as the confessed object of belief

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: alone-word restricting the named divine referent

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is genitive under the preposition but central in meaning: the claim is belief in the named God, not generic deity-language. The name supplies the referent that {{ar:وَحْدَهُۥ}} ({{tr:waḥdahu}}) restricts and that the later pronoun relation keeps in tension. Its worship-authority field survives as pressure, while the local form remains the proper name; the alone-confession also reverses earlier recoil from God alone (39:45; 40:12).

topics.headline: proper divine name, not generic deity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is centered on the named divine referent rather than an abstract or generic deity.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a proper noun in genitive after the preposition.

topics.headline: name anchors exclusivity and pronoun return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine name becoming the hinge for the following alone-word and later pronoun relation.
topics.reason: The following exclusivity phrase refers back to the divine name, and the later pronoun relation keeps that referent in play.

topics.headline: worship-authority pressure retained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices worship-authority pressure around the name, while the local form remains the proper divine name.
topics.reason: The derivational field can add worship and authority pressure, but QAC and local syntax select the proper noun.

topics.headline: alone confession reverses earlier rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this confession of God alone answering earlier recoil from God alone (39:45; 40:12).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references where the same alone-field is contested.

words.gloss_range: accusative circumstantial alone-word with a suffix referring to God
words.root_gloss_range: singleness, aloneness, and making one; locally exclusivity of God within the belief claim
words.prose: {{ar:وَحْدَهُۥ}} ({{tr:waḥdahu}}) makes the claim belief in God alone, with exclusivity attached to the named referent rather than counted separately. It sits as the hinge between affirmation and repudiation: the utterance says alone here, then closes by admitting the speakers had been partner-makers. The same God-alone field reverses earlier refusal in 40:12.

topics.headline: exclusive state of the believed-in referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exclusivity as the state under which God is confessed, not as an independent count-word.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence analyzes the word as an accusative circumstantial element emphasizing God alone.

topics.headline: suffix locks exclusivity to the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exclusivity bound directly to the named divine referent.
topics.reason: The attached third-person suffix refers back to the divine name governed by the belief preposition.

topics.headline: oneness versus partnership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the midpoint alone-word already setting up the final admitted partnership identity.
topics.reason: The later predicate names the speakers as partner-makers, directly opposing the exclusivity marked here.

topics.headline: belated exclusivity reverses earlier response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same God-alone wording now confessed after punishment, reversing the reaction described in 40:12.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete same-surah reference and local timing makes the confession belated.

topics.headline: sound link adds no separate payoff
topics.reason: The sound observation repeats the retained link between exclusivity and the final partnership word.

words.gloss_range: prefixed conjunction coordinating the second declaration inside the quote
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the repudiation to the belief claim with additive contrast. The second declaration is not a separate narrative comment; it remains inside the same emergency quote, so affirmation and rejection stand as a paired reversal.

topics.headline: additive link between opposites
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief and repudiation are coordinated as paired declarations rather than one subordinating the other.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the rejection verb with the belief verb inside the quote.

topics.headline: rejection bound to prior claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices repudiation as visually and syntactically attached to the faith claim, not as a new narrative scene.
topics.reason: The prefixed conjunction attaches directly to the rejection verb and keeps it inside the same direct utterance.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural Form I repudiation with a broad prepositional-relative complement
words.root_gloss_range: covering, denial, unbelief, rejection, and expiation branches; locally direct repudiation of former association, not expiation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: relative pronoun introducing the broad rejected domain

words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرْنَا}} ({{tr:kafarnā}}) gives the quote its negative half: we repudiated. Its complement is the broad {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) plus {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) domain, so the break is not with one named object but with whatever the final predicate will define as former partner-making. The Form I shape keeps the sense as direct rejection, not expiation, and the order makes emergency reversal audible: faith first, rejection second, unlike the pattern of 2:256. Against the partner-language of 40:74, the same field is now voiced as first-person repudiation.

topics.headline: rejection takes a broad complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices rejection aimed at a governed domain rather than at one named idol or object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following prepositional relative phrase the complement of the rejection verb.

topics.headline: completed we-repudiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same group claiming a completed break from its former associations.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect active first-person plural verb, coordinated with the belief claim.

topics.headline: direct denial, not expiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices kufr redirected as disavowal of former objects, while expiation or causative branches are not selected here.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb with a governed complement selects direct rejection rather than a Form II expiation frame.

topics.headline: faith and rejection order becomes emergency syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the unusual emergency order: belief is voiced first, then rejection, unlike the rejection-before-belief pattern in 2:256.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete contrast with 2:256, while local coordination keeps both claims in one quote.

topics.headline: repudiation of former association
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rejection verb pointing toward the former partnership field and the wider verdict language of unbelief.
topics.reason: The complement is defined by the later partner-making predicate, linking rejection to former association.

words.gloss_range: prefixed preposition governing the relative object of repudiation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first-person plural repudiation governing the object-domain
relative pronoun introducing the broad rejected domain

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) after {{ar:كَفَرْنَا}} ({{tr:kafarnā}}) opens the object-domain of repudiation. It is not local or instrumental here; it governs {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) and starts a delayed object whose identity will be supplied by the relative clause.

topics.headline: preposition opens rejection object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rejected material as a governed object-domain of disbelief, not a place or accompaniment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following relative pronoun the governed complement after the rejection verb.

topics.headline: compact object whose identity waits
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the object of repudiation beginning before its content is identified.
topics.reason: The preposition fuses to the relative pronoun, and the defining content comes only in the following relative clause.

topics.headline: second relation prepares third relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated relational prepositions moving from faith, to rejected domain, to former association.
topics.reason: The ayah uses three governed relations in sequence, and this second one opens the domain later resumed by the pronoun.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun introducing the broad domain rejected by the speakers
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is relative here, not interrogative. It keeps the rejected domain open instead of naming particular partners, practices, or mediators, and then lets the following clause define that domain through what the speakers had been. The boundary echo also turns the mocked matter of 40:83 into the rejected domain of 40:84.

topics.headline: relative pronoun, not question word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a rejected domain being introduced, not a question being asked.
topics.reason: The preceding preposition and following relative clause force a relative-pronoun parse in this local frame.

topics.headline: broad domain defined by former identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices names suppressed so the final partner-making predicate can define the whole rejected class.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun begins broadly, and the following clause determines its reference through confessed former practice.

topics.headline: object waits for final identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the listener carrying the object forward until the final identity word lands.
topics.reason: The relative object precedes the clause that defines it, delaying identification until the predicate.

topics.headline: mocked matter becomes rejected domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the object of prior mockery turning into the object of confession and rejection across the boundary with 40:83.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row gives the concrete boundary echo between 40:83 and 40:84.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural defective past verb requiring a predicate
words.root_gloss_range: being, existence, and state; locally former ongoing identity with partner-making as predicate

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition plus pronoun before the final predicate

words.prose: {{ar:كُنَّا}} ({{tr:kunnā}}) turns the rejected domain into a past state: not merely what they did, but what they had been. The clause waits through {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) for the predicate {{ar:مُشْرِكِينَ}} ({{tr:mushrikīn}}), so former identity becomes the definition of what they now repudiate. The simple being-state is not causative formation language; under punishment it also lets their past state sound abased in retrospect. The same we-voice that claimed belief and rejection owns that past identity, with denial fields elsewhere becoming admission here (6:23; 40:73-74; 40:83).

topics.headline: former ongoing state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the admission as a state they had inhabited, not a single isolated act.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the final participle the predicate of this defective verb, producing a past-state construction.

topics.headline: clause waits for predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rejected object being defined through the speakers own former identity.
topics.reason: The defective verb cannot complete the clause without the later predicate, so the final word is structurally necessary.

topics.headline: same we owns past identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same communal voice claiming faith, repudiation, and former identity.
topics.reason: The first-person plural ending matches the earlier quoted perfect verbs.

topics.headline: being-state, not causative formation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices abasement pressure under punishment, while the local verb remains simple being-state rather than causative formation.
topics.reason: The local form is simple defective being, so broader formation or abasement-family senses can only qualify the scene.

topics.headline: denial field becomes admission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices partner-language moving from denial or mockery into first-person admission after punishment appears (6:23; 40:73-74; 40:83).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete nearby and cross-Quran references, while the local quote makes the admission explicit.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus attached pronoun governed by the partner-making predicate
words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) supplies the relation inside the final identity clause. Partner-making is not left objectless: this small fused form carries the preposition and pronoun before the predicate lands. Its referent remains tense against the named God and the broad rejected domain, which fits the offense: attaching partners with Him or through what had mediated that association.

topics.headline: association has a relation object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices partner-making as a relation with an object, not a bare label.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun governed by the preposition with the final participial predicate.

topics.headline: pronoun holds referential tension
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the association problem compressed into a pronoun that can be heard against God and the rejected domain, while syntax keeps it inside the partner-making frame.
topics.reason: The local grammar licenses the prepositional pronoun with the predicate, while the discourse keeps both the divine name and rejected domain close.

topics.headline: small fused relation before identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the relation of offense arriving before the final identity label.
topics.reason: The preposition and pronoun are fused in one word and placed before the final predicate.

topics.headline: third relation completes the chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices relation itself becoming the problem: right attachment, rejected domain, then former association.
topics.reason: The ayah repeats prepositional relation in the belief phrase, rejection phrase, and partner-making predicate.

words.gloss_range: accusative masculine plural active participle as predicate of the former-state clause
words.root_gloss_range: sharing, partnership, and association; locally active partner-making as the confessed former group identity

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: alone-word opposing the final partnership identity
preposition plus pronoun carrying the association relation

words.prose: {{ar:مُشْرِكِينَ}} ({{tr:mushrikīn}}) is the final predicate, grammatically assigning the former identity to the speakers themselves. The root image of sharing is narrowed by {{ar:وَحْدَهُۥ}} ({{tr:waḥdahu}}) and {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) into illicit partner-making: they had made God’s exclusive claim shared. The ayah therefore closes not on their belief claim but on the admitted identity that exposes it, with wider shirk indictment in view (31:13).

topics.headline: final predicate names the speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final identity assigned to the speaking group, not to the rejected domain.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this accusative plural participle the predicate of the defective verb.

topics.headline: sharing becomes illicit partnership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete sharing image converted into theological trespass by the alone-word and the pronoun relation.
topics.reason: The root range includes sharing and partnership, while the local frame with exclusivity and the pronoun makes it culpable partner-making.

topics.headline: ayah closes on admitted identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last word is not the belief claim but the identity they now confess having had.
topics.reason: The final predicate closes the quote and answers the midpoint exclusivity word by opposition.

topics.headline: surah polemic becomes admission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices earlier shirk polemic and grave-injustice language becoming the speakers own admitted identity after divine force appears (31:13).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete broader references, and local grammar makes the admission first-person through the predicate of the we-clause.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The temporal construction links seeing `بأسنا` to the spoken pair `آمنا ... وكفرنا`, while `وحده` and `مشركين` define the two opposed allegiances.
baseline_models.mechanism: Direct perception of overpowering force precipitates a public declaration whose first half assigns exclusive trust to God and whose second half repudiates the former partner-making arrangement.

activation_trace.role: Eye or perceptive seeing supplies the initiating encounter rather than a merely reported warning.
Overpowering severity supplies the coercive object that precipitates the declaration.
Produced speech makes the response an overt and socially audible avowal.
Heart-resting assent supplies the inward content claimed by the spoken avowal.
Divine oneness without partner turns assent into an exclusive allegiance.
Disavowal and disengagement make the second clause a renunciation rather than generic unbelief.
Partner-making identifies the former theological allegiance being renounced.

changed_reading.before: They see punishment, believe in God alone, and reject their idols.
changed_reading.after: The sight of overpowering force triggers an emergency transfer of allegiance: exclusive trust is publicly claimed and the former partner-making relation is expressly disowned.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse moves from sensory `رأوا` through outward `قالوا` to the inward-state verb `آمنا`.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence distinguishes the event that compels speech, the speech act itself, and the settled trust that speech claims. Because force is already visible, the focus alone leaves correspondence between utterance and inward security unresolved.

activation_trace.role: Perceptual seeing supplies the external event that immediately precedes the claim.
Overpowering severity supplies the pressure under which the speech is produced.
Audible utterance marks what is externally established by the verse.
Security and heart-settling name the inward condition asserted but not independently demonstrated.

changed_reading.before: Their belief is simply announced after they see the punishment.
changed_reading.after: Their utterance claims that the heart has settled into security, but the coercive sight-to-speech sequence does not by itself prove that inward settlement.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `كفرنا بما كنا به مشركين` takes the former associated objects or practice as the object of repudiation, opposite `بالله وحده`.
baseline_models.mechanism: A prior state of distributed participation is terminated: the speakers withdraw from what they had made co-participant and replace that arrangement with a sole allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Separation and singleness supply the replacement state of undivided allegiance.
Disengagement and disavowal supply the act that terminates the former relation.
Occurrence in past time locates partner-making as an acknowledged former state.
Participation shared among multiple parties supplies the relational structure being dissolved.

changed_reading.before: They now disbelieve in the beings they once worshipped.
changed_reading.after: They explicitly withdraw from a former shared-allegiance structure and assert a newly undivided relation to God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus confession reverses the exact allegiance pattern stated earlier: in 40:12 God alone was met with rejection and association with assent, while 40:84 joins assent to God alone and rejection to what had been associated. The same lexical poles have exchanged objects only after punishment becomes visible.

activation_trace.role: Assent now attaches to the exclusive divine object.
Oneness without partner defines the newly professed allegiance.
Disavowal now targets the former associated objects or practice.
The old partner-making allegiance is named as the object renounced.
The same exclusive oneness supplies the condition that had previously elicited rejection.
Rejection of the truth supplies the earlier response to invocation of God alone.
Partner-making supplies the earlier condition under which assent was offered.
Assent attached to association supplies the opposite pole of the earlier pattern.

structural_cues: 40:12 and 40:84 share the four allegiance roots but reverse which object receives faith and rejection.
The reversal in 40:84 is temporally subordinated to seeing `بأسنا`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact lexical inversion and the sight-triggered timing; I infer that the later formula exposes a crisis-conditioned reversal of their established polarity. A live alternative is genuine repentance whose lateness, rather than sincerity, is the defect.

changed_reading.before: The speakers formulate a new monotheistic confession under threat.
changed_reading.after: They utter a word-for-word polarity reversal of their prior allegiance pattern, but only when the force they had resisted is directly visible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah stages escalating modes of disclosure: signs are made visible and denied, historical outcomes are available to reflective looking, possessed knowledge becomes an object of boast, and the mocked consequence encloses its mockers. In the focus, seeing finally produces avowal only because disclosure has become bodily inescapable severity.

activation_trace.role: Direct perception supplies the final, coercive mode of disclosure.
Overpowering severity turns disclosure from inspectable evidence into experienced consequence.
Assent is the response that appears only at the terminal evidential stage.
Making visible supplies an earlier divine disclosure that did not require punitive contact.
The opposite of recognition names the refusal applied to already shown signs.
Directed sight or reflection supplies the unused route of learning from prior outcomes.
Claimed disclosure to the knower supplies the self-sufficient epistemic possession displaced by punitive sight.
Descending evil that surrounds its target converts the mocked warning into an enclosing reality.
Mockery supplies the prior stance toward the very consequence that later becomes visible.

structural_cues: 40:81 asks which displayed signs are denied; 40:82 calls for looking at earlier outcomes.
40:83-84 moves without a subject reset from rejoicing in possessed knowledge and mockery to encirclement, sight of severity, and confession.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated disclosure verbs and the immediate 40:83-84 sequence; I infer an escalating evidential threshold in which only experienced consequence defeats denial. The live alternative is that direct sight confirms rather than replaces an earlier intellectual recognition.

changed_reading.before: Seeing punishment supplies convincing evidence and produces belief.
changed_reading.after: Belief appears at the end of a failed disclosure sequence: shown signs, reflective evidence, and warning were resisted until knowledge was displaced by inescapable punitive sight.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier context locates arrogant resistance in the heart or breast and figures it as stamped. That interior obstruction sharpens the focus distinction between what the speakers audibly say and the heart-security denoted by faith: force can reverse speech without demonstrating that the prior interior formation has been undone.

activation_trace.role: Produced utterance marks the externally observable level of the response.
Heart-settling security marks the interior state the utterance claims.
Sealing by a stamp supplies a durable interior obstruction rather than a momentary verbal posture.
The heart supplies the interior site whose state must be distinguished from spoken wording.
Pride and self-magnification supply the resistant disposition associated with the sealed heart.
The breast as the source from which acts issue locates pride beneath outward disputation.

structural_cues: 40:35 places sealing on every heart characterized by arrogance and domination.
40:56 says the disputants carry only pride in their breasts and will not attain its object.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an interior pride-and-seal mechanism and the focus supplies only its speakers' outward claim; I infer that coercion may alter the latter without evidencing removal of the former. The materially live alternative is sincere inward faith that is real but temporally ineffective.

changed_reading.before: The declaration transparently reports a newly believing interior.
changed_reading.after: The declaration is certain as speech but uncertain as evidence of an unsealed, settled heart; the context makes outward reversal and inward transformation separable.

context_deltas.mechanism: Effective response is presented earlier as a turn that continues by following a traversable way, whereas the focus compresses response into an utterance after severity is seen. The next ayah repeats faith, seeing, and severity, negates benefit, and places that negation on a recurring course; correct content has arrived after the interval for enacted following has closed.

activation_trace.role: Assent supplies the correct content whose timing and enactment are being tested.
Following behind supplies duration and enacted continuation beyond an initial turn.
A path extended for travel supplies the practical course on which response must continue.
Benefit as the opposite of harm supplies the expressly negated efficacy of the late response.
The repeated assent root identifies the very faith professed in the focus as ineffective at this point.
Repeated direct seeing pins the loss of efficacy to the same perceptual trigger as the focus.
Repeated overpowering severity fixes the boundary at experienced punishment.
A running, followed course generalizes the closed response window beyond a single episode.

structural_cues: 40:7 coordinates repentance with following God's path before protection from punishment.
40:85 repeats the focus sequence `faith + when they saw + Our severity` and explicitly negates its benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an enacted path model and an explicit terminal non-benefit rule; I infer that the missing element is not correct wording but time for response to become followed practice. An alternative is that lateness alone is decisive regardless of any implied path.

changed_reading.before: The speakers make the right confession, but inexplicably too late.
changed_reading.after: Their formula has correct content but occurs after response can unfold as turning and path-following; experienced severity marks a recurrent closure point at which assent no longer averts harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier judgment-scene answer first locates the associated objects, then erases the past claim with `we were not calling anything`. The focus instead uses the same past-state construction to acknowledge `what we had been associating` before disavowing it. Read thematically, crisis speech moves from disappearance and denial of the objects to ownership and repudiation of the former act.

activation_trace.role: Overt speech supplies the later crisis answer being compared with the earlier answer.
Disavowal supplies an active repudiation that differs from simply denying a past relation.
Past occurrence supplies explicit ownership of a former state.
Shared participation names the former practice that is finally acknowledged.
The interrogation explicitly raises the missing partner-making objects and practice.
Produced speech supplies the earlier defensive answer in the judgment scene.
The same past-state construction is used there to negate rather than acknowledge former conduct.
Calling by speech names the former practice that the earlier answer claims never occurred.

structural_cues: 40:73-74 asks where the associated objects are and answers that they vanished, then says `we were not calling anything before`.
40:84 instead says `what we were associating`, retaining rather than deleting the past-state predicate.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two plural crisis speeches with opposed uses of a past-state construction; I infer a thematic movement from erasure to admission and renunciation. The major live alternative is that the scenes involve different groups, so this is a surah-level speech pattern rather than one group's chronological confession.

changed_reading.before: The final clause merely rejects former objects of worship.
changed_reading.after: The final clause can also mark a late shift from evasively erasing the past to owning the former association precisely in order to repudiate it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads repeated sight language as a political-epistemic mechanism. It remains anchored because 40:29 couples a ruler's `showing/seeing` claim to claimed guidance, while 40:84 uses collective direct sight of God's severity; downstream prose should present this as a possible collapse of mediated vision, not assert that the same speaker or group persists.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The plural `رأوا بأسنا` can contrast unmediated collective sight with the earlier ruler's claim to show others only what he himself sees.

activation_trace.role: Direct collective perception supplies a sight no longer filtered through another speaker's opinion.
Overpowering severity supplies the reality that defeats control over what may be seen.
Showing and making visible supply the ruler's paired claim to control both presentation and perception.
Direction toward a path ties the ruler's curated sight to his asserted monopoly on guidance.

changed_reading.before: A condemned group finally sees divine punishment.
changed_reading.after: Their collective direct sight may also stage the collapse of an earlier regime in which authority claimed to determine what others could see and treat as guidance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the hunter's snare image within `شرك`. It remains anchored to `مشركين`, the disavowal branch of `كفرنا`, and exclusive `وحده`; downstream prose should render it only as a material analogy for desperate extrication, not as the lexical sense of the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: `وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين` can carry an exploratory image of trying to disengage from an entangling partnership only after overpowering danger is seen.

activation_trace.role: A hunter's entangling snare supplies the exploratory material image of the former association.
Disengagement and renunciation supply the attempted motion out of that entanglement.
Separation and singleness supply the claimed state after extrication.
Overpowering severity supplies the moment when the entanglement is recognized as fatal.

changed_reading.before: The speakers renounce their former partners.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the speech resembles a last attempt to cut free from an entangling partnership at the instant its fatal capture becomes visible.

strongest_changes: The exact inversion of 40:12 turns the focus confession into a delayed reversal of an established allegiance polarity.
The 40:81-84 disclosure sequence distinguishes signs and reflective evidence from the coercive sight that finally defeats denial.
The path model of 40:7 and the explicit ruling of 40:85 show why correct confessional content can arrive after its effective response window.
Heart-and-seal cues preserve a live distinction between an outwardly certain declaration and an inward transformation that the declaration alone cannot verify.
summary.what_was_special: The focus reuses the surah's own faith, rejection, oneness, association, sight, and severity roots in a tightly reversed formula, and the following ayah repeats the sight-triggered faith event while directly denying its benefit.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not decide whether the declaration lacks inward sincerity or is sincere but temporally ineffective.
The 40:73-74 denial-to-admission pattern may connect distinct condemned groups only thematically.
The curated-vision and snare models are useful cross-domain activations but should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Direct sight abruptly dissolves partnership.** `ر ء ي/B001` supplies sensory seeing or insight, `ب ء س/B001` overwhelming force, and `ش ر ك/B001` shared participation. The temporal “when” makes sight the trigger for exclusive faith. I infer that coercive visibility removes the ambiguity that sustained partners; confession reads as evidentially correct but temporally compelled.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The final ayah corrects any assumption that accurate confession is sufficient: when overwhelming sight causes it, the earlier trust-function cannot be recovered.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Visible force compels the correction that clear demonstrations did not elicit.** Lexically, `ب ء س:B001` is "severe force or punishment," `ر ء ي:B001` seeing by eye or insight, `و ح د:B004` God's exclusive oneness, and `ش ر ك:B002` associating a partner with God. Structurally, 40:83 shows clear proofs rejected within a closed knowledge-system; only when force is seen do the speakers affirm oneness and disavow partnership, while 40:85 says that assent no longer benefits. Force's role is to make consequence perceptually unavoidable. The packet gives the timing; I infer that this recognition is now coerced by realized harm rather than freely responsive to signs. The content is corrected, but the mode and moment of correction disable its saving function.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:85 decisively corrects any content-only reading of faith: the proposition is now right, but its timing and coercive evidentiary mode leave it functionless.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği görsel ya da içsel algıdır; belirli söz öbekleri ve bakma çabası ayrı kullanımlar olarak tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın görme çekirdeği ile doğrudan göz tanıklığını ve görmeye çalışma bildiren bağlı kullanımlar birbirine karıştırılmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ortak ekseni, bir konu hakkında zihinsel bir yargı veya görüş oluşturmaktır. Bilme ya da sanma değeri belirli tümce yapılarında, danışma ise başka birinin görüşünü istemede ortaya çıkar; bunlar yalın çekirdeğin eş düzeyli anlamları sayılmamalıdır.
